records.learner: The panels live in a private bucket, and storage rules block direct reads for every user, so the only way to an image is through our API route. That route checks the session and whether the user has access to that chapter, and if yes, the server signs the file path with a 120-second expiry and returns it with Cache-Control: no-store. The reader asks for links panel by panel as you scroll, so a scraper only holds a few links, and the signed links rotate every two minutes, so old ones stop working. That's why the real protection is on the server, not in the browser.
records.planted_point: Says the signed links 'rotate every two minutes' as if a global timer refreshes them; the correct version is that each link expires 120 seconds after it is signed, generated per panel on demand.
records.tutor: Feedback: You said the links rotate every two minutes; each link expires 120 seconds after it is signed. You didn't mention that every table requires Row Level Security for full server-side enforcement. Since the server handles access, what happens if a user tries to call the API route directly without being logged in?

answer_errors: Says the signed links 'rotate every two minutes' as a global timer, instead of each link expiring 120 seconds after it is signed, generated per panel on demand.

records.learner: So the iframe sends a postMessage to our page, and we listen for it, but only accept it if the origin is exactly Centrobill's domain and the data has the shape we expect. But that message never unlocks anything by itself — it just tells the screen to check again, and we show 'confirming your payment' for a second or two. The real unlock happens when Centrobill's server sends the postback to our server, we verify it there, and then we write the access row in Supabase, using the service role key on the server side. So a forged message from the console can't buy a chapter.
records.planted_point: Says the postMessage listener verifies the origin and then the access is written after the server postback — mostly right, but implies the browser message is part of the unlocking flow ('check again' then unlock) rather than strictly: the postMessage only refreshes the UI, and access is granted solely by the verified server-to-server postback writing the row.

And I remember there's also something about storing votes per week so the reset doesn't delete anything, but honestly I haven't thought through that part much.

records.learner: Yes, that's fine. Uploads go straight to the private bucket, and the heavy work — resizing and cutting the pages into vertical panels — runs in a background job, not inside a single server function, so a big batch never blocks a request. Each panel is processed as its own task, and if one fails it's retried without redoing the whole upload. The creator sees the progress in the portal, and the chapter only goes live when every panel is ready.

records.learner: Sure. It's five weekly milestones plus a QA week, and every Wednesday the code is on your GitHub and on Vercel staging. Week one is the foundation: the full schema in Supabase, Row Level Security on every table, the 45/55 split, and the private buckets. Week two is protection — the 120-second signed links, the protected reader, and the Sunday leaderboard reset. Week three is the creator side: the upload portal, the AI scan, and the auto-cropping into vertical panels. Week four is payments: the Centrobill iframe and postback, the paywall at chapter four, and the 18-plus gate. Week five is payouts and revenue: the Paxum ledger, the ad slots, and the print-on-demand webhooks. Week six is only testing and polish, with sign-off on December 24th.

records.learner: So every sale is stored in cents as whole numbers, never decimals, because floating point drifts. Then one database function writes both rows, the platform 45% and the creator 55%, in the same transaction, so either both are written or none. For the rounding, we pick a fixed rule, for example the extra cent goes to the platform, and apply it always, so the two rows add up exactly to the sale.
records.planted_point: The lesson's must-say for payments: that the browser message never unlocks anything (access is only granted after server-side verification of the postback).
records.tutor: Feedback: Your approach to handling rounding with fixed rules guarantees perfect accuracy in the ledger. Now, some US states, like Utah, expect real age verification for adult content. How would you handle that?
